❓Can Supply Control — SOP & rules
Can Supply Control — Standard Operating Procedure
Raw-material can planning · Alamance Foods · supplied by DS Containers (DSC)
Prepared by
Bala Pradeep Konda
Senior Sales & Operations Analyst
What this tool does. It plans how many raw cans (item codes starting 12) we need to buy from DSC, and when — by taking demand from three sources in priority order (firm sales orders → production plan → forecast), netting it against on-hand stock and open purchase orders, and flagging every can that needs an order, an expedite, or a swap. Every page below is a different lens on that same live calculation. Click any can # on any page to open its full dossier.
🆕 Recent logic updates (Oct 2026) — so the team shares one source of truth:
  1. Physical counts are reference-only. The on-hand used for every calculation is always the NetStock figure; a physical count and its date are shown alongside (📋) with the variance, for spotting discrepancies — they never drive the math.
  2. Item transitions fire on "Ready to order = Yes." Order-placed is ignored. While ready-but-not-complete it rolls (deplete the old can first, order the new can for the rest); "Transition complete = Yes" switches the item fully to the new can.
  3. Truck size is per-can. A trailer holds 50 pallets, so a big (13oz) truck = 95,000 cans and a small (6oz) truck = 114,000 cans (2,280 × 50). Orders bigger than a truck are split across trucks.
  4. Cans with no ounce size default to LARGE (13oz). If a can's description has no "oz", it's planned as a big can (pallet 1,900, truck 95,000).
  5. Expedite + new PO together. When a late inbound PO is expedited but still leaves the can below its cover target, the residual is also placed as a new PO — both actions are shown, not just the expedite.
  6. LTO rule. LTO cans are ordered on firm PA + the production plan only; leftover forecast never triggers a callout (details below).
  7. Committed plan is checked gross — including firm PA inside it. The production plan is a confirmed build: the line consumes a can per case for the full plan, regardless of finished-goods (FG) stock OR of firm sales orders that sit inside the plan. Two things that used to quietly shrink the plan's can demand are now fixed — (a) FG on-hand no longer nets against the plan, and (b) firm PA that the plan already builds is counted in the plan layer instead of being carved out and then erased by FG on-hand. FG on-hand still nets forecast, and firm orders beyond the plan. Result: the dossier's "Production plan" coverage now equals the Consumption Planner grid, so the true shortfall is always flagged and ordered for (previously a plan could read "short 1,600" or even "covered" when the grid showed it short 17,000+ — worst on LTOs with FG stock).

📊 Board — the daily action list

What it shows: every can grouped by urgency — stocked out, expedite, order now, this week, upcoming, covered — plus the ready-to-place PO list, POs to swap, and the "talk to DSC" list where firm PA is at risk. How we use it: this is the start-of-day screen. Work top-down: clear stockouts and expedites first, place the POs in the order list, action the swaps, then capture the day in the tracker. Filters at top (size, LTO, customer, and the policy inputs — lead, buffer, MOQ, truck, min/ideal/max days) apply everywhere.

🗓 Consumption Planner — where the demand comes from

What it shows: each can's consumption by fiscal week or period, from today forward, with projected end-of-bucket balance (red = shortfall) and the Σ horizon total. How we use it: to see when a can gets consumed and whether on-hand + POs carry it through each week — the demand story behind the board's order timing. The over-ordered panel at the bottom flags cans past the 60-day max and suggests swapping that capacity to a short can.

📦 Order Schedule — the forward buy plan

What it shows: for every can that needs ordering in the next 180 days, each order's place-by date → delivery date → quantity → what it covers, sized to reach the Ideal days of supply and never exceed Max. How we use it: to plan DSC orders ahead, not just today's — hand DSC a forward calendar of what's coming and when.

🛡️ Coverage Runway — position vs policy

What it shows: where each can sits right now inside its Min→Max days-of-supply band — green bar = on hand, blue = on order, dashed lines = Min and Max. How we use it: a health check to spot cans below Min (order) or above Max (over-bought) at a glance. Click a can # for its dossier, or click the row to expand the drivers inline.

📸 Daily Tracker — trend over time

What it shows: a snapshot each day of the key counts (POs to place, expedites, swaps, over-ordered, stocked out, talk-to-DSC) with trend lines. How we use it: capture the board each day; the charts show whether we're working the plan down over the week. Snapshots save in this browser and can be exported or backed up to a file.

🔮 Forecast — how the forecast plays out

What it shows: each can's demand straight from the Forecast file (forecast × BOM cans-per-case), by fiscal period — independent of the production plan — with how far on-hand + POs cover it. LTO items (Limited Time Offers, from the BOM's UDF_LTO flag) are shown in purple and get a two-order buy plan: a first buy at LTO start and a second later, split by the adjustable % at the top (default 50/50). How we use it: to pressure-test forward demand and plan LTO buys off the forecast rather than the plan.

🏭 Production Plan — cans the build will consume

What it shows: the 13-week finished-goods production plan exploded into weekly can consumption (plan cases × BOM cans-per-case), with how long on-hand covers each. How we use it: to order cans against the committed build. Cans on the plan are also ordered for on the Board. The Order-spread view recommends how to spread orders to hold a target weeks-of-cover.

⚖️ Capacity Plan — leveling against DSC capacity

What it shows: demand leveled against DSC's weekly production capacity, flagging weeks that exceed capacity, plus a PO plan sized to a target weeks-of-cover. How we use it: to check DSC can physically make what we need each week, and to spread orders so no single week is infeasible.

🔎 The item dossier — click any can #

What it shows: for one can — supply on hand, days of supply, DSC floor stock, and three headline coverage points (Firm PA covered, Production plan covered, Forecast days of supply), followed by the plain-English "why," key dates, demand drivers, open POs, and the firm PA sales orders behind it. How we use it: the single source of truth for one can when someone asks "why are we ordering this / when do we run out."

🔄 Item transitions (old can → new can)

Transition gate — "Ready to order" drives it: the moment Ready to order = Yes, we start ordering the new can. Order placed (Yes/No) is ignored. While ready but not yet complete the transition is rolling — the old can's on-hand is depleted first, then the new can is ordered for the rest (the old can is not re-ordered). Once Transition complete = Yes (the new BOM has been created), the new can fully owns the item's demand. If Ready to order is still No, nothing changes — all demand stays on the old can and it is ordered normally.

🟣 LTO items (Limited Time Offers)

Bought once, up front — not reordered off forecast. For an LTO we buy the whole run at the start (planned on the 🔮 Forecast page as the B1/B2 two-buy split) and let it deplete. So on the Board an LTO can is ordered on firm PA + the 13-week production plan only: whatever forecast is left on it never triggers an order callout — it stays informational on the Forecast page. But a shortfall still flags: if firm PA is not covered, or the production plan is not covered, the LTO can is flagged and ordered exactly like any other can. The suggested quantity covers only that uncovered PA/plan — it is not padded with forecast runway. LTO cans are marked 🟣 purple everywhere, from the BOM's UDF_LTO flag (a combo counts as LTO if either variant is).

This walks through a single real can from today's data, step by step, so a new team member can see exactly where each number comes from and how it turns into an order decision. Load your files and the example uses a live can; otherwise it shows an illustration.

Reference — rules & definitions

Data sources

  • Stock on Hand (NetStock) — can on-hand, per-item lead time, safety stock, and NetStock's own status (Ok / Potential s/o / Stocked out…).
  • Live PA — finished-goods on hand (Q.O.H.) and every open sales order with its ship date. INVENTORY placeholder lines (cust 9999 / year 2055) are ignored.
  • Purchase Orders — open can PO lines (ordered − received, converted THOU → cans) with required dates.
  • Can Inv Count — physical on-hand counts (Date · Item Code · Total Count). The physical count and its date are shown for reference on each counted can (📋 chip + in the can detail); the board's on-hand math always uses the NetStock figure. Variance of the physical count vs NetStock is shown so you can spot discrepancies.
  • Forecast + BOM — built in. Forecast is in cases; the BOM explodes each finished good into cans (≈12.24 cans per 12-pack case incl. scrap).
  • DSC Floor Stock — the "Alamance Detailed Inventory On Hand" pivot from DSC: can codes in column A, quantities by year/period. The current-period column (e.g. 2026-08) is read as DSC's floor on hand; the row Grand Total is kept as "all lots". If DSC's floor covers a can's full need, the quick-turn lead is applied automatically (DSC✓ chip) — which pulls that can out of urgent ordering.

Demand & timing math

PA first, forecast second. For each finished good: firm Live PA orders are consumed against FG on hand in ship-date order. The first order that FG stock cannot cover sets the production start. If no firm shortfall exists, forecast coverage (FG on hand ÷ daily forecast) sets it. Daily can burn = current + next period forecast, exploded through the BOM.
  • Runs dry — day the can balance goes negative with no new supply.
  • Need-by = runs-dry date − production buffer (default 7 days, so production always has a week of cans ahead).
  • Last day to order = need-by − lead time. Standard DSC lead is 28 days; cans on the Floor stock @ DSC list use the quick-turn lead (default 7 days) instead.
  • Run-out (with POs) — same simulation but including open PO arrivals on their required dates. Overdue POs count as arriving today but are flagged.

Status boxes

  • Stocked out — zero cans, consumption already running, nothing arriving within 3 days.
  • Expedite PO — a PO exists but its first arrival lands after the need-by date: pull the PO in. If pulling it in still leaves the can below its cover target, a new PO for the residual is also recommended.
  • Order today — last safe order day is today or already past.
  • This week / Next week / Upcoming — last safe order day in 1–7 / 8–14 / 15–28 days (or a NetStock flag).
  • Covered — no action inside the horizon.

Priority queue

All urgent cans ranked by the earliest firm PA order at risk (chip shows P8 PA / P9 PA); forecast-only cans rank after all PA-driven ones. The queue drives both swaps and the PO plan.

Stale backorders

Two kinds of PO lines are ignored entirely — excluded from incoming supply, coverage, run-out math and swaps: (1) stale backorders, overdue by more than Ignore POs overdue days (default 3); and (2) short-ship remnants, lines with less than Ignore PO remnants cans left open (default 5,000) — the small leftovers when DSC delivers slightly under the ordered quantity. Both appear in the "Ignored POs" box with a reason, ready to be verified and cleared from the system.

Swap rules

DSC's six swap rules — every recommended swap must satisfy all of them:
  1. No swaps inside 12 days — DSC needs a 10-day production lead + 2 transit days. The donor PO must be at least the No-swap window (default 12d) out.
  2. Same size only — a 13oz-big donor can only cover a 13oz-big need, a 6oz-small only a 6oz-small. Never across sizes.
  3. No floor-stock items — floor-stock cans (quick-turn) are never swapped, on either side.
  4. No flexed-in items — cans listed in the Flexed-in cans box are excluded from swaps.
  5. Similar quantities — the amount pulled in may exceed the donor PO by at most Swap qty tol (~8 pallets). Sacrificing the other way (give up more than you pull, e.g. 95,000 out to pull 15,200 in) is always fine; pulling in far more than you give up (15,200 out for 95,000 in) is not.
  6. Job for job (1:1) — one donor PO for one order. The tool never splits one donor across two needs. Pushing two jobs to pull one in is a manual, case-by-case call with DSC.
A can that needs cans but has no rule-compliant donor is placed as a new PO instead, with the reason shown.
On top of the DSC rules, a swap is only proposed when it is meaningful:
  • The urgent can must have a firm PA shortfall — forecast-only demand never takes a swap slot.
  • The urgent need must be ≥ Min swap qty (default 20,000 cans) — no swapping for 2–3k-can needs.
  • The donor PO sits on a can that is fully covered (no production need in 180 days) or arrives ≥ 14 days early, is itself ≥ Min swap qty, and is due before the urgent can's need-by.
  • Each donor PO can be claimed by only one urgent can. Remaining need after a swap flows into the PO plan.

PO builder rules

  • A PO fills toward one full truck — a trailer holds 50 pallets, so big (13oz) = 95,000 cans, small (6oz) = 114,000 cans. Orders larger than a truck are split across trucks.
  • Every line is at least the MOQ and a whole number of pallets — big (13oz) = 1,900 per pallet, small (6oz) = 2,280 per pallet. Partial pallets are never sent, orders never fall below the MOQ, and only same-size cans share a truck. A can whose description has no ounce size is treated as big (13oz).
  • Needs are packed in queue priority order; one item can span multiple POs, and one PO can mix items.
  • A short final truck is topped up by pulling next week's needs forward (lines tagged PULLED FWD). If nothing can be pulled, the truck is marked PARTIAL — top it up or hold it.
  • POs to place now = contain items whose last order day is ≤ 2 days out; next week = 3–14 days.
  • Expedite + new PO together: a can with a late inbound PO is expedited — but if pulling that PO in still leaves it below its cover target, the residual is also placed as a new PO (the line is tagged "⚡ also expedite PO ####"). Only when the inbound PO fully reaches the target is no new PO placed. Swap-covered quantity is deducted first.

Swap decisions — the DSC round-trip

Swaps here are proposals until DSC agrees. Export the Swap decision template from the swaps section, have DSC mark each row YES or NO in the Decision column, and drop the file back onto the board (✅ Swap Decisions tile). YES rows lock in and show ✔ CONFIRMED BY DSC. NO rows stay visible with a red ✖ NO — DECLINED BY DSC indicator: the board then recommends the next-best donor PO as an ↻ ALTERNATIVE PO (clearly marked, with the declined PO named on the card), or — if no other covered PO qualifies — the urgent can's need automatically flows into the new-PO plan, where the line is tagged ⇄ swap declined by DSC → new PO so you can trace exactly where it went. A declined donor PO is never proposed again, even across repeated decision uploads (decisions merge, they don't overwrite). Blank rows stay proposed. Removing the file (✕ on the tile) returns everything to proposed.

Customer filter

Pick one or more customers (from Live PA order lines) in the 👥 dropdown. The whole page then shows only cans tied to those customers' firm orders, and the queue, swaps and PO plan are ranked by their orders. Forecast burn rates stay whole underneath so run-out dates remain realistic. Clear returns to all customers.

On-hand policy — days of supply (all customers)

At the top set the global Min days (floor), Ideal days (the target we order up to), and Max days (ceiling) of supply. Every can is planned to these unless a customer or can overrides them: order sizing aims for the Ideal days and never exceeds Max; anything below Min is flagged.

⬇ Export policy (in the floor-stock row) downloads a simple file with one row per customer and four columns: Customer, Ideal days of supply, Minimum days of supply, Maximum days of supply. Edit the numbers, save, and ⬆ Import policy — every can that serves a customer is re-planned to that customer's days-of-supply policy. Leave a customer blank to use the generic top-of-dashboard defaults. Co-manufacturing customers default to the tighter co-man band. Standard lead time (28d), buffer (7d) and cover still apply.

Co-manufacturing customers — low-inventory band

Some customers (default Conagra, Rubix, Danone, Nestle) are co-manufacturing accounts where we deliberately hold very little stock. In the 🤝 bar up top you can add or remove customers (matched by name, case-insensitive) and set the Min and Max on-hand days (default 7 and 14). Any can that feeds one of these customers' finished goods is flagged 🤝 CO-MAN and held to that tight band: its order sizing uses the MAX-day window as its cover instead of the standard cover, so it's never overstocked, and it's still ordered a week ahead. The 🤝 Co-manufacturing section shows every co-man can with its on-hand, current days-of-supply and band, colour-coded BELOW MIN / IN BAND / OVER MAX. Standard 28-day lead time is unchanged; floor-stock cans follow their own quick-turn rule.

⬇ Co-man on-hand plan exports one row per customer × can with on-hand, daily use, days of supply, and the MIN/MAX day band (and the equivalent MIN/MAX on-hand in cans). Edit the MIN/MAX day columns for any can, save, and ⬆ Import adjusted bands — those per-can bands override the global default and the board re-plans instantly.

Everything exports

Every box, the queue, the swap list, the PO plan and every single can exports to Excel with the action and full reasoning included.

Consumption Planner page

The 🗓 Consumption Planner tab (top-left) breaks the same live production need down by fiscal week or fiscal period (2026 calendar: P1–P12, 4/5-week periods, embedded). It auto-detects today's period and week, highlights the current bucket, and shows per-can consumption, incoming POs and the projected end balance per bucket — red when a shortfall is projected. The current bucket counts remaining days only. Search and the customer filter apply here too, and the whole grid exports to Excel.

Lead times, buffer, truck size, MOQ, min-swap and the floor-stock list are all editable at the top — the whole board recalculates instantly.
